cards.explanation: The answer is light. The man says, "He has driven me away and made me walk in darkness instead of light." (Lamentations 3:2) He's not just sitting in a dim room, friends. He says he's been walking in it. I think this is a man who's tired of not being able to see where he's going.

The answer is bitterness and hardship. The man says, "He has besieged me and surrounded me with bitterness and hardship." (Lamentations 3:5) A siege means being closed in on every side, and he says bitterness and hardship are on all of them. I think that's a heavy way to be hemmed in.

The answer is False. The man says, "He has walled me in so I cannot escape; He has weighed me down with chains." (Lamentations 3:7) He says he cannot escape, so he's not slipping out whenever he likes. Walls around him and chains weighing him down, and I think that's a heavy spot to be in.

The answer is that God shuts out his prayer. The man says, "Even when I cry out and plead for help, He shuts out my prayer." (Lamentations 3:8) Notice he's still crying out and still pleading. I think that tells you how much he needs help, even while it feels like the door is closed.

The answer is crooked. The man says, "He has barred my ways with cut stones; He has made my paths crooked." (Lamentations 3:9) Stones in the way, and the paths bent on top of that. Not even a map app could sort that out, friends.

The answer is lying in wait for him. The man says, "He is a bear lying in wait, a lion hiding in ambush." (Lamentations 3:10) Both animals are waiting and hiding, ready to spring. I think that's how it feels to him, like danger could jump out at any moment.

The answer is target. The man says, "He bent His bow and set me as the target for His arrow." (Lamentations 3:12) A target is the thing everything's aimed at. I think that's about as exposed as a person can feel.

The answer is True. The man says, "He pierced my kidneys with His arrows." (Lamentations 3:13) The arrow from the verse before has landed in his own telling. I think this one hurts, friends, and it's okay to say so.

The answer is False. The man says, "My soul has been deprived of peace; I have forgotten what prosperity is." (Lamentations 3:17) Peace is gone, and so is his memory of prosperity. I think that's a lonely place to be.

The answer is hope. The man says, "My strength has perished, along with my hope from the LORD." (Lamentations 3:18) His strength is gone, and he says his hope from the LORD is gone with it. I think this is the lowest thing he says so far.

The answer is that his soul remembers and is humbled within him. The man says, "Surely my soul remembers and is humbled within me." (Lamentations 3:20) After everything he's listed, his soul still remembers and is humbled. I think that's an honest thing to say out loud.
